title: Skipping a fixed head literal in the term sub-tree
statement: Let $\rho$ be a restriction on $n$ variables, let $l$ be a literal whose underlying variable $v$ is not free under $\rho$ (that is, $\rho$ already assigns $v$ a fixed Boolean value), let $\mathit{rest}$ be a list of literals, and let $\mathrm{cont} : \mathrm{Restriction}\,n \to \mathrm{DecisionTree}\,n$ be a continuation. Then the sub-tree built for the term $l :: \mathit{rest}$ under $\rho$ with continuation $\mathrm{cont}$ coincides with the one built for $\mathit{rest}$ under $\rho$ with the same continuation; the fixed head literal $l$ contributes no branch.
hypotheses_covered: l.var is not a free variable of ρ
l is a literal on n variables
rest is a list of literals
cont is a continuation from restrictions to decision trees
ρ is a restriction on n variables
replaced:
When the head literal $l$ is not free in $\rho$, it is skipped:
$\mathrm{termSubTree}\,(l :: \mathit{rest})\,\rho\,\mathrm{cont} = \mathrm{termSubTree}\,\mathit{rest}\,\rho\,\mathrm{cont}$.
